metadata.title: Sorting People by Age
metadata.description: Sort (name, age) pairs by numeric age using sorted() with a lambda key.

instructions.main: Given `people = [("Sam", "9"), ("Ada", "41"), ("Bo", "35")]` — ages stored as text — sort the pairs youngest-first into `sorted_people` with `sorted(people, key=...)`.
steps: Ages are strings, so convert inside the key: `key=lambda person: int(person[1])`.
`sorted(...)` returns a new list — leave `people` unchanged.

hints.message: Start with `sorted_people = sorted(people, key=lambda person: int(person[1]))`.
The key returns the text "9", "41", "35" — compared as text, "9" sorts after "41". Wrap the age in `int(person[1])` so ages compare as numbers.
Use `sorted(...)` — it returns a NEW sorted list. `.sort()` reorders `people` in place and returns None.

evaluation.feedback_on_all_pass: You sorted the pairs youngest-first with a numeric sort key.

test_cases.feedback_on_pass: sorted_people orders the pairs youngest-first: Sam, Bo, Ada.
test_cases.feedback_on_fail: sorted_people must be [("Sam", "9"), ("Bo", "35"), ("Ada", "41")] — sort the ages as numbers, not as text.

test_cases.feedback_on_pass: You used sorted() with a key lambda.
test_cases.feedback_on_fail: Build the result with `sorted_people = sorted(people, key=lambda ...)` — `sorted(..., key=...)` returns a new list; `.sort()` mutates the original.
